messages.content: Your answer must contain at least two sentences ending in a period followed by at least two bullet points denoted by *. Consider a directed weighted graph G(V, E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges. Suppose we use adjacency list to implement the graph. Consider a sequence of |V| operations with each corresponding to a different vertex in V. For the operation for vertex v, the cost is assumed to be the number of outgoing edges from v.  (a) What is the cost of the worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations? (b) What is the average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis?

message.content:
The worst possible single operation can cost |E|, because one vertex could have all the outgoing edges in the graph. The total cost over the sequence of |V| operations is the sum of all outdegrees, which equals |E|, so the average amortized cost is |E|/|V|.

* (a) The worst-case single-operation cost is |E|.
* (b) The aggregate-analysis amortized cost per operation is |E| / |V|.
